title: Rapid seller triage: pocket deck for pilot incidents (in-review)
content:
Purpose: fast pocket-deck for sellers/SEs to triage pilot incidents during first 30 days. Not a formal runbook — quick actions, scripts, talking tracks, and escalation lanes.

Audience: SEs, sellers running customer pilots, field ops on-call.

Slide 1 — TL;DR (30s opener)
- Goal: keep pilot running and preserve customer confidence while ops investigates.
- Key levers: divert traffic, fall back to cheaper/older model, throttle batch size, enable prefix-cache, escalate to concierge.
- When to call SRE: repeated SLO breaches for >3 minutes or repeated 5xx spikes >2% of requests.

Slide 2 — Quick triage matrix (Decision-first)
- Symptom: latency spike (p95 > target)
  - Immediate: switch routing policy to low-latency variant OR region fallback (console → Route override).
  - Short-term: drop batch window from 100ms→30ms; reduce concurrency on client side.
  - Talking track: "We're temporarily routing to a low-latency variant to keep interactive flows snappy — we'll revert after warmup."
- Symptom: cost surge (unexpected tokens/retries)
  - Immediate: enable token caps per request, enable dedupe/caching for repeated prompts, set short-term quota.
  - Talking track: "We've temporarily capped token usage for the pilot to stabilize cost while we audit prompt patterns."
- Symptom: model quality regression
  - Immediate: fallback to previous pinned model version; enable deterministic sampling (top_p 0.0/top_k small).
  - Short-term: run evals on the failing prompt set, capture examples, open regression ticket.

Slide 3 — Rapid commands & console pointers (copy-paste)
- Console: Admin → Routing → Add override (customer-pilot-id) → target: model-variant-lowlatency → TTL: 15m
- CLI: redwoodctl rollback --pilot customer-pilot-id --to-version v1.3.4 --reason "rapid fallback: quality regression"
- Throttle API: curl -X POST $REDWOOD_API/quotas -d '{"account":"cust-x","max_tokens":50000,"window":"1h"}' (note: replace with tenant id)

Slide 4 — Customer-facing micro-scripts (use in-call)
- Latency: "We saw a latency blip and routed to a lower-latency variant to preserve interactivity. No data was lost; this is a temporary change while we investigate."
- Quality: "We observed a change in outputs on a narrow set of prompts and will temporarily pin the prior model while the team runs a targeted regression check. We'll share examples and remediation ETA."
- Cost: "We've applied a short-term guardrail to reduce unexpected token usage during the pilot — it's reversible and we'll share transparent logs."

Slide 5 — Escalation lanes (who to ping)
- Level 0 (seller/SE): handle immediate routing and talk-track. Slack channel: #pilot-triage.
- Level 1 (field ops): @Priya for routing/console ops; handle quota/override cleanup.
- Level 2 (serving runtime): @Jordan (applied-ml) for kernel/latency anomalies and KV cache warmup checks.
- Level 3 (SRE/ops): oncall SRE if incident >15m or customer in SEV-2. Use incident template: CONCIERGE-TRIAGE-INCIDENT (link in linked_artifacts).

Slide 6 — Checklist for a 15-minute stabilization window
- 0–2m: confirm symptom, pick single mitigator (routing override or rollback).
- 2–5m: apply mitigator, notify customer with micro-script, start capturing example traces.
- 5–10m: monitor p50/p95/p99 and error rates; if improving, schedule follow-up postmortem; if not, escalate to Level 2.
- 10–15m: either revert mitigator with customer consent or escalate to SRE.

Slide 7 — Common pilot gotchas (field notes)
- Large system prompts + long context → KV cache thrash → p95 spikes. Mitigator: reduce prefix length + warmup cached prefixes.
- Unexpected looped retries from client SDKs producing token storms. Mitigator: throttle retries and set idempotency keys.
- Quantized model mismatches for specific tokenization (non-UTF8 edge cases). Mitigator: pin CPU tokenization and add test cases.

Slide 8 — Example mini-postmortem template (fill fast)
- Customer, pilot id, start/end times, symptom summary (1 line), mitigation applied (with timestamps), root cause hypothesis (1–2 lines), next actions + owner.
- TODO: link to lightweight template in Confluence (CONFLUENCE:INF-TRIAGE-827).

Slide 9 — Risk/objection scripts (procurement / security)
- Procurement: "We provide temporary quotas and transparent logs; for pilots we recommend a capped reserved seat to avoid surprises."
- Security: "Private pilot data can be routed to a dedicated VPC or ephemeral private deployment for PII-sensitive workloads — recommend SRE onboarding."

Slide 10 — Open questions / TODOs (notes to self)
- Add short-runbook commands for Dedicated console (Priya to add).
- Validate CLI command formats with release-engr (Evan) — potential flag changes in v0.18.
- Capture 3 canonical customer examples of model-regression and add to example library.
- Add a 1-page printable card for sellers (fit to 1-a4).

Appendix — quick reference snippets (crib sheet)
- Best fallback choices by symptom: latency → lowlatency-variant; quality → pinned-version; cost → token-cap; outages → region-fallback.
- Slack templates: "@field-ops quick triage needed for pilot cust-###: p95 spike → routing override applied, monitoring. TL;DR: ETA 15m."

Notes: this is intentionally terse. Will iterate into a printable pocket deck for sellers + a lightweight Confluence page. Do not publish externally until we standardize wording with Legal (procurement scripts).

Linked tickets/refs: see linked_artifacts above.

End of draft.
